$comment: Scraping configuration: the identity pool and the whole-IP request budget.
All traffic leaves from this machine's own ISP connection — no proxies.
See README, section 'Identity pool & IP caps'. Every key is optional.
Override the file path with SCRAPING_CONFIG=/path/to/file.json.
This file is the LOCAL HIGH-THROUGHPUT profile: per-request identity
rotation, a large pool, and an adaptive rate that finds this connection's
real ceiling instead of assuming one. config/scraping.conservative.json
holds the cautious defaults if you want to fall back to them.

connection.$comment: home | office. Affects warnings only, never behaviour.

$comment: count: pool size. Each identity is a consistent browser persona with its
own headers, TLS profile, cookie jar and referer chain.
rotation: 'per-request' draws a different identity for every fetch;
'sticky' keeps a product with the identity that fetched it last.
minGapMs: minimum spacing between ONE identity's requests. This is what
bounds pool throughput: capacity ≈ count × (60000 / minGapMs.max) per min.

cycle.$comment: Requested window per cycle, seconds. Stretches if the budget cannot fit the products.

$comment: mode 'adaptive': dayPerMin is only the STARTING rate. The controller adds
one request/min per clean interval and multiplies by decreaseFactor on any
hard block, settling where this connection actually tolerates. The global
pause is reserved for being blocked while already at minPerMin.
mode 'fixed': dayPerMin/nightPerMin are hard limits, never exceeded.
tolerateBlockRatio: share of recent requests that may be blocked before the rate is cut. A lone block among hundreds is noise, not congestion.

night.$comment: IST hours during which the night ratio applies and the pool thins out.

$comment_noiseRatio: Fraction of fetches that browse a homepage/search page INSTEAD of a product, varied +/-50% at runtime. Real sessions are mostly NOT product pages; a feed that is ~98% product detail pages has a composition no household produces.
$comment_maxConcurrent: Requests in flight at once across the pool. One per identity regardless. Must be high enough that maxConcurrent / avgFetchSeconds >= target rate per second.

limits.$comment: refuseWhenStretched: stop at boot when the catalogue stretches the cycle past 3x. Off here — a long cycle is expected at this scale.

$comment_funnelRatio: Fraction of product fetches that arrive via a search results page (the most common real path to a PDP). Costs one EXTRA request each — volume is what gets metered, so this buys traffic shape at a price.
